content_preview.title: TIOBE Index August 2026: MATLAB Exits the Top 20 for the First Time in Over a Decade as Rust Holds No. 10
content_preview.summary: TIOBE's August 2026 index kept Rust at No. 10 and pushed MATLAB to No. 25, its first finish outside the top 20 in more than 10 years.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

TIOBE's August 2026 programming-language popularity index left its top 10 in the same order as July, but MATLAB fell to No. 25, marking the first time in more than 10 years that the language has finished outside the top 20, according to [TIOBE](https://www.tiobe.com/tiobe-index/) and [InfoWorld](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4207496/matlab-programming-language-sinking-in-popularity.html). Rust, which entered the top 10 for the first time [in July](/article/2026-07/14-tiobe-index...

editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (status 200, no suspicious_patterns) and read in full from the gzipped snapshots on disk after verifying each file's sha256 against manifest.json (all three matched: source-0 a2c24cd4..., source-1 7c8082cd..., source-2 b940b1ee...). source-0.html.gz (tiobe.com/tiobe-index/, the official TIOBE index page): confirmed the full Aug 2026 top-10 table verbatim (Python 18.53%, C 11.10%, C++ 8.62%, Java 8.25%, C# 4.09%, JavaScript 2.63%, Visual Basic 2.18%, SQL 1.88%, R 1.56%, Rust 1.45%, with Delphi/Object Pascal at No. 11 on 1.37%), the Aug2025-vs-Aug2026 rank columns (confirming Rust moved from No. 18 to No. 10 and C moved +2.07 points), MATLAB at No. 25 on 0.71%, and all four Paul Jansen quotes used in the article ('Is this just a temporary dip... MATLAB's days are numbered', the MATLAB-licensing quote, the Delphi-paid-license quote, the 'language from another era' quote, and the OCaml/Zig 'may become new top-20 entries' quote) — every one verbatim. source-1.html.gz (techrepublic.com, Liz Ticong, Aug 11 2026): confirmed verbatim the two quoted phrases attributed to TechRepublic ('well ahead of every other language despite a 7.61-point decline in its rating from August 2025' and 'the only language among the current top five to post a year-over-year increase'), the C++/Java 0.37-point gap framing, the Rust 'largest jump of the three... gaining eight places since August last year' quote, and the MATLAB 'recover at least five places from its ranking this month' quote. source-2.html.gz (infoworld.com/Paul Krill, Aug 10 2026): confirmed the same top-10 list and percentages independently, MATLAB ranked 25th and 'fallen out of the top 20 for the first time in more than 10 years', and the same Jansen quotes reproduced by InfoWorld. All three sources independently corroborate the core numbers, so there is no single-source risk on any load-bearing fact. All specifics (percentages, ranks, point gaps, the 'eight places' / 'five places' figures) were independently re-derived from the raw tables and checked against the article's arithmetic — all correct.

Every numeric specific (ranks, percentages, point deltas, the 0.37-point C++/Java gap, the 0.08-point Rust/Delphi gap) was independently recomputed from the raw TIOBE table and matches. No hallucinated figures or misattributed quotes found. The headline and lead claim ('MATLAB Exits the Top 20 for the First Time in Over a Decade') is directly supported by both TIOBE ('for the first time in more than 10 years') and InfoWorld ('for the first time in more than 10 years') verbatim.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism, no editorializing beyond the clearly-labeled Analysis section, no AI self-reference. Attribution phrasing ('according to,' 'per') is used consistently and correctly maps each claim to its actual source.
